title: Lease token metadata protocol for interrupted client streams
creator: Ava Martinez
description: When clients disconnect mid-generation (network blips, process exit, mobile pause) we retain partial generation state (KV prefix cache, output buffer, cost tracking). Current GC policies are conservative and either leak short-lived state or aggressively purge resumable output, causing poor UX and cost surprises. This ticket defines a lightweight lease token metadata protocol to: 1) provide a short-lived, signed lease that encodes minimal metadata needed to safely identify and resume/cleanup partial generations, 2) enable deterministic server-side garbage collection without guessing client intent, and 3) support an opt-in reconnect path that is compatible with hosted and Dedicated deployments. The protocol prioritizes minimal storage overhead, privacy (no PII in tokens), and replay resistance via HMAC + rotating keys.
acceptance_criteria: Server issues a signed lease token and expiration to client for long-running streaming generations
Partial-generation state is retained only while a valid lease exists or supervisor indicates client expected to reconnect
Reconnect handshake accepts lease token and reconciles prefix cache + token cursor to resume with low duplication risk
GC worker purges partial state after token expiry + soft grace window and emits metrics/events
No PII or full request payloads encoded in token; replay attacks mitigated with HMAC key rotation policy
Integration tests simulate disconnects and verify resume/cleanup semantics under load
implementation_notes: API: streaming endpoint adds optional response header 'x-rw-lease' with base64(signed_metadata) and 'x-rw-lease-expiry' UTC timestamp
Client: on reconnect clients may present 'x-rw-lease' in initial POST to request resume; server validates HMAC and checks cursor validity
Server-side state: store minimal mapping keyed by lease-id -> {cursor_hash, model_variant, cost_counter, last_seen_ts}. State size targeted < 1KB per lease by design
GC: periodic GC worker deletes state once expiry + configurable grace window elapses; before final delete emit 'lease_expired' event to audit log
Security: sign tokens with KMS-backed HMAC key; include key-id version so we can rotate keys without invalidating active leases until a rollover window
Privacy: do not include raw prompt or user identifiers in token. Use stable, opaque cursor_hash to allow collision check on resume without exposing payload
Backward compatibility: if no lease header is exchanged server behaves as today (stateless abort), making this opt-in per-client or per-route
Dedicated/Private: lease metadata stored in customer-scoped store (etcd or redis namespace) for isolation and exportability during migrations
testing_plan: Unit tests for token signing/validation and expiry boundary conditions
Integration tests: simulated client disconnects mid-stream and reconnect with valid lease -> expect resume and no duplicated tokens
Chaos test: randomly kill client connections at high QPS and assert GC rate and memory overhead remain within SLO
Load test: create 1M ephemeral leases over 24h on staging to validate GC throughput and storage growth
Security test: key rotation simulation to ensure old leases validate against previous keys when within rollover window
E2E UX test: client library sample performs resume flow and recovers from mobile sleep with <1s additional latency
dev_updates: 2026-02-15: Ticket created. Initial problem statement and goals added by Ava Martinez.
2026-02-18: Design sync with runtime and infra teams. Decided on HMAC-signed opaque token rather than server-only monotonic lease to reduce coord load.
2026-02-22: Security reviewed high-level approach; requested KMS integration and key-id in token to support rotation (action: JAMAL to add KMS plan)
2026-02-27: Implemented prototype token issuer in server sandbox. Observed token validation adds ~200ns p99 to handshake. Punchlist: optimize base64 and reduce metadata to cursor_hash only.
2026-03-01: PM feedback (Riley Chen): make opt-in via route config and surface lease expiry in Console dashboards. Added labels for console telemetry
2026-03-03: Blocker discovered: Dedicated deployments need tenant-scoped lease store. Infra to scope redis namespaces (ENG-33411). Rolling work into dependencies.
2026-03-05: Prototype tests show GC worker can purge 50k expired leases/s on staging-n2. Next: add audit events and integration tests. Assigned to Jamal Singh for implementation phase.
notes: Trade-offs considered: server-only lease (less client complexity) vs signed token (lower server coord cost). Chosen: signed token to reduce runtime centralized state under high QPS.
Potential follow-ups: expose a 'lease-health' metric per-tenant for Dedicated to tune grace windows, and integrate with Console's rollout controls to opt-in routes gradually.
Open question: default grace window. Proposal: 30s for mobile-first routes, 5s for low-latency public endpoints. PM to decide per-route defaults.
QA: ensure token replay from different client IPs fails unless other safety checks pass (cursor_hash match).
